Seminar Title:

GAI-Driven Multilingual Audio Semantic Communication Framework for 6G Applications

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Arvind Yadav ( Rollno : 524ec1009)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room (EC303)

Date and Time:

16 Oct 2026 10:00 AM

Contact:

Anirban Bhowal

Abstract:

Conventional audio communication networks deliver all bits precisely, leading to wastage of bandwidth and latency that become a bottleneck for future 6G technologies like autonomous cars, virtual reality, and smart cities. In this report, we present a novel framework of GAI-powered multi-language semantic audio communication based on the paradigm shift from precision at the bit level to the preservation of semantic information. The framework includes a semantic encoder based on HuBERT architecture along with FiLM-conditioning, a dynamic multilingual KB, an importance-weighted channel encoder focusing on semantically vital bits, and a GAI decoder that is capable of decoding the message even in low SNR wireless channels. A set of exhaustive experiments on the Google FLEURS dataset was performed for three languages (Hindi, English, French), three channel models (AWGN, Rayleigh fading, Rician fading), and several SNRs from -10 dB to 20 dB. The performance was measured with eight different criteria for acoustic quality (PESQ, STOI), semantic similarity (SIM, SIS, SD), and linguistic accuracy (WER, CER, BERT). According to experimental results, the proposed system delivers an average PESQ of 1.777, STOI of 0.831, SIM of 0.747, and BERT score of 0.856 and consistently outperforms the semantic baseline without GAI (PESQ: 1.719, BERT: 0.854) and far exceeds the traditional QPSK-MMSE baseline (PESQ: 1.378, BERT: 0.612). &nbspThe proposed system reaches 66.9\% of Oracle PESQ ceiling (2.657), which proves that the current system architecture is capable of extracting almost all possible performance within the constraint of 16 kHz HiFi-GAN vocoder.
